_comment: An OpenHCL IGVM whose VTL0 is OUR guest -- the isolation/m3 monitor image -- instead of the
OpenVMM project's test kernel and initrd. Built by build-ownguest.sh, which supplies the
resources file; see that script for what each resource is and where it comes from.
The VTL0 command line is the one the Windows launcher passes today for a partition
(windows/vbslike/host/src/launcher.rs): the m3 init reads report_host= to find the launcher's
signing service, and the console goes to ttyS0 so the partition's COM port carries it.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DECIDE, and must not be read as deciding: the trust configuration. This
is the kernel-hashes shape -- a paravisor above our guest, no SVSM beneath it -- in which the m3
monitor's configfs-tsm report path still exists. A COCONUT-bearing configuration is a different
thing with different digests, and on that path the guest's VMPCKs are being removed, so the
monitor must move to an SVSM protocol before it works there (isolation lane, 2026-09-23). One
image never implies one trust configuration.
